title: Strata Systems - POC scoping (open models)
summary: POC scoping for open-model shortlist for Strata Systems (geospatial analytics). Discussed success criteria (latency, hallucination rate, throughput), benchmark plan (500 prompt eval, bilingual coverage), timeline (2-4 week pilot), model shortlist (Llama2-70B, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B, RedPajama variants), hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), security and compliance asks, and concrete next steps: share pricing/POC template, security pack, and run initial benchmark on sample prompts.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Grace Lee (Redwood AE), Markus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Strata - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Diego Ramirez (Data Eng)

Auto-summary: quick scoping — Strata wants to validate open models for PROD-level geospatial QA and user-facing summarization, needs benchmarks for latency, hallucination control, and bilingual output (en/es).

[00:00] Grace Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Grace from Redwood, this is Markus Chen our SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Aisha Patel: Good thanks, Aisha here. Super excited to talk through the POC.
[00:09] Liam O'Connor: Liam, hi. Quick note — we only have about 45 minutes, hope that's okay.
[00:13] Grace Lee: Perfect. Outline — success criteria, workload sizing, models we recommend for an open-model POC, and timeline. Then we can capture next steps.
[00:20] Markus Chen: Quick intro from our side on how Redwood typically runs an open-model pilot — we normally do a 2-4 week bench and a short production validation, we can run on Hosted API initially then move to Dedicated or Private depending on regs.
[00:30] Diego Ramirez: Sounds good. Our main driver is replacing a brittle rule-based summarizer for geospatial incident reports and building an in-app Q&A. Latency and hallucination are the two big flags.
[00:39] Grace Lee: Good, can you quantify latency targets and throughput?
[00:42] Aisha Patel: Ideally p50 < 200ms for short prompts (<=250 tokens) and p95 < 600ms. Throughput — about 150 requests per minute at peak for pilot, production could be higher. Cost target is more of a soft constraint: we want to be < 0.8x of current ops cost but quality must improve.
[01:05] Markus Chen: Okay that helps. For hallucination control what's an acceptable rate? Do you have an eval metric?
[01:10] Aisha Patel: We have an internal annotator set; we'd like factuality > 92% on our 500 sample prompts and fewer than 5% critical hallucinations on edge cases.
[01:20] Grace Lee: Great. So success criteria: latency, throughput, factuality threshold, and bilingual quality for English/Spanish. We'll include hallucination metrics in the benchmark.
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: Also security — we need SOC 2 type II, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, and KMS integration. Potentially a VPC option if we go private.
[01:41] Grace Lee: Yep we can send the security pack. Redwood Private supports VPC and customer-managed KMS. We'll attach SOC2.
[01:47] Diego Ramirez: On data residency, some customers in LATAM require EU-region hosting — can you pin regions?
[01:53] Markus Chen: We can route to region-specific capacity and pin models to regions; we'll note that in the POC template.

[02:10] Markus Chen: Now model shortlist. For open-models we typically run 3-4 variants to evaluate latency/quality tradeoffs. Based on your geospatial summarization and bilingual needs, recommended shortlist: Llama2-70B (instruction tuned), Mistral-Instruct (chatty but cheaper), Falcon-40B, and a RedPajama-3B variant for fast inference/edge baseline.
[02:35] Aisha Patel: Curious on why Llama2-70B vs Mistral — any expected quality gaps for factuality?
[02:40] Markus Chen: Llama2-70B generally gives strong instruction following and factual grounding with larger context handling, Mistral-Instruct has strong cost/latency profile and performs well on many instruction tasks but may need prompt engineering to reduce hallucinations. Falcon-40B is a middle ground, and RedPajama variants give a low-cost baseline but expect lower fidelity on edge-case domain facts.
[03:05] Grace Lee: We'll also test quantized variants (8-bit and 4-bit where applicable) to reduce cost but monitor quality delta, and consider KV cache behavior for longer sequences.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: For multilingual Spanish we need to be careful — any of those show big drops?
[03:20] Markus Chen: Llama2 and Mistral both handle Spanish okay, but we should include Spanish prompts in the 500-prompt set and measure BLEU-ish style or human eval for fluency/accuracy. Falcon sometimes needs more instruction priming.

[04:00] Diego Ramirez: Example workload: average request 180 tokens in output, 120 tokens input. We expect prefix caching to help for repeated queries — is that supported?
[04:10] Grace Lee: Yes Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. For repeated geospatial context we can benefit a lot — we'll suggest caching config in the benchmark.
[04:18] Markus Chen: Also we'll measure token costs and ops — batching, concurrency, and the smart router can fall back to cheaper model if the higher tier is saturated. For the POC we can simulate peak traffic.

[05:00] Aisha Patel: On benchmarks — what's a realistic plan?
[05:03] Markus Chen: We propose a three-stage benchmark: 1) functional evaluation on your 500 prompts (mix en/es, domain edge cases), 2) throughput/latency tests (1000 concurrent synthetic requests to model the peak), 3) long-tail tests focusing on hallucination using adversarial prompts. We'll provide scripts and an evaluation sheet.
[05:26] Grace Lee: Timeline wise, if you can share prompts by 2026-03-22 we can start hosted benchmark week of 2026-03-23 and have initial results by 2026-03-27. If you want Dedicated capacity we'll size and price it in parallel.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: That timing works. Can you run a cost comparison hosted vs dedicated for the pilot numbers?
[05:45] Grace Lee: Absolutely — we'll send both numbers and a projection for production at 3x pilot load.

[06:10] Aisha Patel: A few technical Qs — model quantization support, GPU types you use for dedicated, and how you measure p95 latency with batching?
[06:18] Markus Chen: Quantization: we support 8-bit and selected 4-bit paths depending on model. We benchmark both to show quality delta. Dedicated runs on A100/H800 equivalents; we pick kernels by architecture and sequence length. For p95 we run realistic concurrency with our continuous batching engine and report observed p50/p95/p99.
[06:39] Diego Ramirez: Any gotchas around KV cache invalidation when we pin model versions?
[06:44] Markus Chen: Not really — KV cache is per-instance and tied to model version; if you roll models we invalidate cache unless you configure warmup/replication. We'll show best practices.

[07:20] Aisha Patel: Regarding data — will training or fine-tuning be part of POC? We mostly want inference, but might consider small fine-tune if quality is low.
[07:28] Grace Lee: For this POC we recommend inference-only. If we see quality issues we can discuss lightweight fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation as next phase.

[08:00] Markus Chen: One more practical item — evaluation metrics definitions. We'll use: factuality percentage (human-labeled), token cost per request, p50/p95 latency, throughput (req/min), and a small human-fluency score for Spanish output. We can add a hallucination-severity rubric.

[09:10] Liam O'Connor: Are there any known limitations with Llama2 licenses for production?
[09:15] Grace Lee: Llama2 has a permissive license for commercial use, but we'll include recommended compliance notes in the security pack. We'll also list model provenance and vetting info.

[10:00] Aisha Patel: Ok, can you summarize tradeoffs for model shortlist?
[10:05] Markus Chen: Sure — Llama2-70B: highest quality, higher cost/latency; Mistral-Instruct: competitive quality with better cost, may need prompt tuning; Falcon-40B: middle ground; RedPajama small: low-cost baseline for high concurrency but expect fidelity loss. We'll include quantized variants in the bench.

[12:30] Diego Ramirez: For the bench infra do you need us to open ports or provide account keys?
[12:36] Grace Lee: For hosted bench we just need sample prompts and a test API key we'll issue with rate limits. For Dedicated we would need account and network peering details later.

[13:05] Aisha Patel: One more ask — can you run an adversarial test for hallucinations? We have about 50 tricky cases.
[13:12] Markus Chen: Yes please include those in the 500 set and mark them as adversarial. We'll run a separate analysis.

[14:00] Grace Lee: Quick recap and next steps: Grace will send POC template, pricing, and security docs by Friday 2026-03-20; Markus will propose benchmark config and a hosted vs dedicated cost comparison by 2026-03-25; Aisha will provide the 500 prompt set (including 50 adversarial) by 2026-03-22. We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff week of 2026-03-23.
[14:28] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[14:31] Aisha Patel: None from our side, just internal approval on budget but timeline is firm.
[14:36] Grace Lee: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and attach the docs.
[14:40] Diego Ramirez: Thanks all.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present in audio — model names sometimes mis-attributed (e.g., red pajama vs redpajama), some filler words omitted.

End of transcript.
